title: Entropy-driven kernel hinting and soft-padding guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, experimentally-driven design for routing requests to kernels and choosing padding budgets using a notion of shape entropy. The goal: reduce wasted compute from over-padding while keeping scheduling complexity manageable and preserving latency SLOs. This is intentionally a pragmatic proposal for short-term rollout (canary in prod) and includes telemetry hooks and rollout criteria.

Motivation / Observed problems:
- Long tail of sequence length distribution increases average padding if we naively batch to max length.
- Current length bucketing is coarse and causes mixes of incompatible sequences that either increase latency (waiting) or waste tokens (padding).
- Kernel performance varies nonlinearly with shape (seq_len x batch_size x KV locality). Some kernels are better for many-short vs few-long.
- KV cache warmup and eviction interplay with padding: over-padding can sneakily cause more KV thrash for long-running conversations.

Core idea (high level):
- Compute a small "shape entropy" score per request based on short-length histogram hints and token-profile features. Shape entropy = measure of unpredictability of sequence length within a short time window / route.
- Use entropy + simple heuristics to emit a 2-bit kernel_hint and a 1-byte padding_budget value per request. Kernel_hint drives late-binding kernel selection without bloating scheduler state. padding_budget is the max allowed pad tokens to add when grouping into a micro-batch.
- Keep buckets coarse (3-5 runtime bins) but allow runtime to form ephemeral micro-groups using kernel_hint and pad_budget, enabling more aggressive packing for low-entropy traffic and conservative behavior for high-entropy/interactive traffic.

Request-side metadata (what we attach):
- shape_entropy (float, quantized to 0-255 client-side)
- median_prefix_len (uint16) — median of recent sequences for same session/route when available
- kernel_hint (enum: fast-short, balanced, long-tail) — derived server-side if client not providing
- pad_budget (uint8) — max pad tokens budget for grouping
Note: clients may supply basic histogram hints for large-batch producers; otherwise server computes quick estimate from the first token blocks.

Kernel_hint semantics and mapping: 
- fast-short: prefer kernels optimized for high throughput at short seqs (low KV overhead). Favor vectorized attention kernels, high-ALU occupancy.
- balanced: default kernel, safe across shapes. 
- long-tail: choose kernels that scale with long sequences (streaming-friendly, KV-friendly, lower activation memory).
Mapping to existing kernel pool is via a lightweight name -> capability list stored in runtime config.

Padding budget policy (soft-padding):
- pad_budget is a max per-request pad allowed. Runtime may choose smaller pad if better pack forms.
- Soft-padding means we allow adding pad tokens up to budget but never exceed latency deadline. We compute an optimistic pack score: saved_token_work = (tokens_padded_outside - tokens_added_by_padding) * kernel_cost_factor. Only commit pad if optimistic score positive and estimated latency within SLO.
- Default budgets by kernel_hint: fast-short -> 8 tokens, balanced -> 32 tokens, long-tail -> 128 tokens. These defaults are tunable per-tenant.

Micro-grouping rules (ephemeral):
- Scheduler opportunistically forms micro-groups from requests matching same kernel_hint and similar median_prefix_len (within 16 tokens by default).
- Max micro-group lifetime 20ms, unless deadline relaxation explicit.
- If shape_entropy <= low_threshold, allow cross-median mixing to increase batch size; if > high_threshold, avoid waiting and send as-is.

KV cache interaction and prefetching heuristics:
- When using long-tail kernels and pad budgets that increase apparent sequence lengths, we mark those micro-batches for "pre-warm" KV allocations to avoid transient thrash.
- Prefetch policy: when a session shows repeated long requests, proactively allocate a KV segment on the GPU node at the next request. Mark TTL of pre-warm entry to 5000ms.
- Eviction hint: micro-groups with conflicting pad_budget and kernel_hint should not share KV entries unless same session id.

Telemetry and rollout metrics (must be instrumented):
- pad_tokens_added_ratio: tokens_added_by_padding / total_output_tokens per route
- kernel_hint_success_rate: fraction of requests where chosen kernel hit target latency and throughput
- micro_group_utilization: mean batch_size for micro-groups vs baseline bucket groups
- kv_warmup_hit_rate: fraction of long-tail requests that hit pre-warmed KV segment
- tail_latency_p99 and p999 per route; these gate canary expansion

Experiment plan (quick A/B):
- Phase A (simulation): run offline replay of 7 days of traffic, calculate theoretical savings and risk.
- Phase B (canary 1%): enable shape_entropy compute and pad_budget emission only; runtime still uses balanced kernel but logs decisions. Observe telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Phase C (canary 5%): enable kernel_hint->kernel selection for micro-groups, monitor p99 and kernel_hint_success_rate.
- Phase D (ramp): if p99 stable and pad_tokens_added_ratio < baseline, ramp to 25% and then 100% with gradual pad_budget tightening.

Microbench notes (early runs):
- On A100 tests with transformer-xl-like model, grouping by kernel_hint reduced wasted pad tokens by ~18% and improved throughput by ~6% in mixed workloads.
- KV pre-warm decreased initial-step latency for repeated long sessions by ~12% in the bench cluster.
- Fast-short kernels saw 0.5% p99 increase in highly bursty traffic when pad_budget > 16; suggests conservative default for interactive routes.

Operational concerns and fallbacks:
- If kernel hinting causes any p99 regression > 5% on canary routes, auto-disable hinting for that route and emit an alert.
- Ensure ability to force route-level policy: e.g., tenant config can pin kernel or disable soft-padding.
- Cost visibility: add per-route delta report for token-work saved vs added by padding.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the cheapest, privacy-safe way to compute shape_entropy for privacy-sensitive routes? (Option: compute quantized metric server-side only and do not persist.)
- How to integrate with existing routing policies (region/cost/priority) without blowup of combinatorial states? (Idea: kernel_hint as orthogonal dimension for best-effort grouping only.)
- Explore ML-based pad_budget predictor for high-volume tenants.

Action items:
- Spike: implement shape_entropy estimator (Marcus) by 2024-11-20 and add replay tool integration.
- Telemetry: add pad_tokens_added_ratio and kernel_hint_success_rate (Elena) by 2024-11-30.
- Bench: run 3 model families (LLama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-70B-stub) for microbench and produce result table (Chris) by 2024-12-10.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a practical, small-surface change to enable improved packing without requiring heavy rework of the scheduler. The design emphasizes conservative defaults and fast rollback. Please focus review on the telemetry contract and the pad_budget thresholds per route.

End of document.
